note: Everything the companion assumes rather than takes straight from the PDS. In data and code, mark the words that rely on one as {{id:the words}}; the page shows them with a red dotted underline and a hover-over. 'pds' says what the PDS (or ATO) does state; 'check' says how to settle it.

items.title: Counting the days for a pro-rata minimum
items.assumed: In a financial year with 29 February, the days in the year are taken as 366. (Counting both the start date and 30 June is shown by the PDS example.)
items.pds: The PDS example counts 273 days from 1 October 2026 to 30 June 2027 out of 365. It doesn't show a leap year.
items.check: Confirm the leap-year treatment against the admin system.

items.title: Counting the days when a pension closes mid-year
items.assumed: The pro-rata minimum on closure counts the days from 1 July (or the start date) to the closure date, both included.
items.pds: The PDS says a pro-rata minimum may still need to be paid on closure, but not how the days are counted.
items.check: Confirm the day count before quoting an amount.

items.title: How many payments are left this year
items.assumed: Monthly, quarterly and half-yearly payments are counted from the start month to June, assuming the first payment falls in the start month.
items.pds: The PDS gives the payment months, says payments are made by the 28th, and spreads Bryn's TTR income over April to June. It doesn't give a cut-off for a payment in the start month.
items.check: Use 'Payments left' to override it if the first payment is later.

items.title: Fortnightly payment count
items.assumed: Without a known payment date, one fortnightly payment every 14 days is assumed.
items.pds: The PDS says fortnightly payments are made by every second Friday, but not which Fridays.
items.check: Enter any past fortnightly payment date for an exact count.

items.title: Rounding each payment
items.assumed: Each payment is rounded to $10: up for the minimum (so the year adds up to at least the minimum) and down for the TTR maximum.
items.pds: The PDS rounds the yearly minimum to the nearest $10, and the Bryn example rounds $13,333.33 a month to $13,330. It doesn't say how each payment is rounded.
items.check: Confirm the per-payment rounding against the admin system.

items.title: Using an age instead of a date of birth
items.assumed: An age on its own is taken as the member's age on the pension start date.
items.pds: The minimum percentage depends on age at the start and then each 1 July, which needs the date of birth.
items.check: Use the date of birth for anything near a birthday or 1 July.

items.title: What counts as a business day
items.assumed: Business days are Melbourne business days: weekends and Victorian public holidays are skipped.
items.pds: The PDS says 'business days' for withdrawals and cooling-off, and 'Melbourne business day' for investment switches.
items.check: Confirm for timeframes that aren't investment switches.

items.title: Victorian public holidays
items.assumed: Holidays are worked out by rule. Anzac Day has no substitute when it falls on a weekend, Melbourne Cup day is a holiday, and the Friday before the AFL Grand Final only counts once it's added to holidays.json.
items.pds: Not covered by the PDS.
items.check: Check the Victorian Government's published holiday list each year.

items.title: Day counts are calendar days
items.assumed: Timeframes given in days (complaints, 90-day windows, 180-day insurance windows) are counted as calendar days.
items.pds: The PDS gives these as a number of 'days' without saying calendar or business days.
items.check: Confirm if a deadline is close.

items.title: Division 293 estimate
items.assumed: Uses the member's income plus this year's concessional contributions (or the amount they're on track for).
items.pds: The ATO's Division 293 income also includes reportable fringe benefits and net investment losses, and the ATO works out the tax after the year ends.
items.check: The ATO's assessment is the real figure.

items.title: LISTO estimate
items.assumed: Uses the member's income as adjusted taxable income and this year's concessional contributions so far.
items.pds: The ATO assesses eligibility (including a 10% employment income test) and pays it after the year ends.
items.check: The ATO decides the amount.

items.title: Co-contribution estimate
items.assumed: Uses the member's income as 'total income' and this year's personal contributions so far.
items.pds: The ATO requires the member to be under 71 at the end of the financial year, and has other eligibility tests on its co-contribution page.
items.check: The ATO decides the amount after the tax return is lodged.

items.title: Measuring inactivity
items.assumed: Months without activity are counted from the last contribution date.
items.pds: Insurance stops after 16 consecutive months without a contribution or rollover. The inactive low-balance rule says an account is 'inactive for a period of 16 months' without listing what counts as activity.
items.check: Check the account history for rollovers and other activity.

items.title: DASP six-month date
items.assumed: The visa has already expired or been cancelled by the six-month date. (Counting six months from departure is in the PDS.)
items.pds: The PDS says super not claimed within six months of departing Australia is transferred to the ATO; the visa must also have expired or been cancelled.
items.check: If the visa ended after departure, check which date applies.

items.title: Spouse eligibility for a split
items.assumed: Uses the spouse's age and whether they're recorded as retired; their preservation age comes from their date of birth.
items.pds: The spouse must be under preservation age, or between preservation age and 65 and not retired.
items.check: Confirm the spouse's work status with the member.

items.title: When carry-forward is mentioned
items.assumed: Only raised for members who are working and either earn $100,000 or more or are making personal contributions.
items.pds: Carry-forward needs a total super balance under $500,000 at the previous 30 June; the unused amount is shown in ATO online services.
items.check: The member checks their available amount in ATO online services.

items.title: Order of checklist steps
items.assumed: Steps are in a suggested call order.
items.pds: The PDS only fixes some of the order: a notice of intent must come before a contribution split, rollover, withdrawal or pension start, and a split before a rollover.
items.check: Reorder to suit the call.

items.title: Online account menu names
items.assumed: Menu names are read from the online account's link addresses.
items.pds: Only four account paths are stated in the PDS (Manage account, Personal details, Pension payments, Your Insurance).
items.check: Confirm the exact labels while logged in.

items.title: Adult children and death benefit tax
items.assumed: Adult children are usually not dependants for tax purposes.
items.pds: For tax, a child must be under 18, or be financially dependent or in an interdependency relationship at the date of death.
items.check: Check the actual circumstances at the date of death.

items.title: Example figures
items.assumed: With no member loaded, figures use an example balance of $500,000 at 5%.
items.pds: These match the PDS 'Gavin' example, not any member.
items.check: Load a test member or use the drawdown calculator for real figures.

items.title: Pension start date in the month figure
items.assumed: The month figure assumes the pension starts on the 1st of the chosen month.
items.pds: A pension can start on any day; the minimum is pro-rated by days.
items.check: Use the drawdown calculator for an exact start date.

items.title: What changes the transfer balance account
items.assumed: A lump sum from a retirement pension (a commutation) reduces the amount counted against the cap. Regular pension payments, and investment growth or losses, don't change it.
items.pds: How super works (p17) says the transfer balance account tracks "debits and credits" but doesn't list them.
items.check: Check the ATO's transfer balance account pages, or the member's transfer balance account in ATO online services.

items.title: Split contributions and the concessional cap
items.assumed: Contributions split to a spouse still count towards the member's own concessional cap, and not the spouse's.
items.pds: How super works (p10 to 11) covers who can receive a split, the 85% limit and who owns it, but not how the caps treat it.
items.check: Check the ATO's contributions splitting page.

items.title: When bring-forward starts
items.assumed: Bring-forward starts automatically in the first year a member under 75 goes over the annual non-concessional cap.
items.pds: How super works (p13) gives the bring-forward amounts and periods; the ATO says the arrangement "allows you to bring forward" future years' caps.
items.check: Check the ATO's non-concessional contributions cap page, and the member's bring-forward status in ATO online services.

items.title: What makes up each tax component
items.assumed: The tax-free component is mostly after-tax (non-concessional) contributions; the taxable component is employer, salary sacrifice and deducted personal contributions, plus earnings.
items.pds: The PDS (Flexi Pension p29, How super works p18) says a benefit has both components and how each is taxed, not what goes into each.
items.check: The member's actual components are on their statement.

items.title: Examples of compassionate grounds
items.assumed: Medical treatment, palliative care and mortgage arrears are among the grounds the ATO accepts.
items.pds: The PDS says compassionate grounds are applied for with the ATO, without listing them.
items.check: Check the ATO's compassionate grounds page for the full list and the evidence needed.

items.title: Ending one job when there are others
items.assumed: Ending an employment arrangement on or after 60 releases the balance at that point even if the member keeps or starts another job.
items.pds: The PDS lists "ceasing an employment arrangement on or after reaching age 60" as a condition of release, without covering other jobs.
items.check: Check the ATO's 'When you can access your super' page.

items.title: When a timeframe starts
items.assumed: The day the timeframe is counted from, where the PDS gives the length but not the starting point.
items.pds: The PDS gives these periods without saying exactly when they start.
items.check: Confirm the starting point with the team that handles it before quoting a date.
